jobs.title: Manager, FP&A - Customer Care
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future.

Vivint Smart Home, an NRG owned company, is a leading smart home company in the United States, dedicated to redefining the home experience with intelligent products and services. We find purpose in proactively protecting and keeping our customers connected to home, no matter where they are. Join the Smart Home team to create smarter, safer and more sustainable homes.
Summary:

This role is responsible for managing financial and business analyses in support of the Vivint Customer Care business (Call Center). Working closely with business leaders and FP&A leadership, this role leads monthly and quarterly variance analysis and coordinates annual budgets, long-term plans, and recurring forecasts.

Primary Responsibilities:

- Own and coordinate Customer Care operating expense budgets, forecasts, cost analyses, reporting needs, and ad hoc requests (including forecast inputs into the Financial Planning and Reporting system).

- Develop monthly actuals and forecast variance analyses used to complete the monthly business review.

- Prepare monthly, quarterly, annual, and ad hoc reports for senior leadership and executive management.

- Continuously improve reporting and analysis to provide clearer insight into financial performance and support business growth.

- Partner with business leaders to develop reporting that increases clarity and supports informed operating decisions.

- Respectfully challenge current financial, reporting, and operational processes.

- Lead or support special projects assigned by management.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Business, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline.

- Five or more years of financial analysis experience (Corporate Finance, FP&A, Accounting or related fields (Operations or Call Center experience preferred).

- Proficiency with reporting and financial systems (e.g., SAP, FPR, HFM, Adaptive, Snowflake SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI) as well as high proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

- Strong personal code of ethics and demonstrated ability to maintain confidentiality.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

- Maintains a high level of curiosity and determines why results occurred and how the business should adjust, not only what happened.

- Works independently with initiative and self-motivation while collaborating effectively in a highly matrixed stakeholder environment.

- Adapts effectively to new and changing environments.

- Works effectively in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, multiple assignments, and a high degree of accuracy.

- Quickly conceptualizes and assimilates data to derive insight and take appropriate action while maintaining a broader business perspective.

- Builds positive stakeholder relationships, communicates effectively with varied audiences, influences decisions, and challenges constructively.

- Connects financial performance to operational and industry factors.

- Mindset to challenge ideas, make data-driven decisions, and think like a consultant.

Why Join Vivint:

Learn about the Vivint Culture and why it’s a great place to grow your career! Here are some highlighted perks you should ask us about:

- Free daily lunch and drinks onsite.

- Paid holidays and flexible paid time away.

- Employee, friends, and family discounts.

- Onsite health clinic, gym, and recreation amenities.

- Medical, dental, vision, and life coverage, plus a 24/7 medical hotline.

- 401(k) plan with employer match.

- Employee Resource Groups.

Working Conditions:

- Ability to Work onsite in Lindon, UT Monday-Thursday; flexible onsite/remote work on Fridays

This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, monitors, phones, photocopiers, and AV conference room equipment.

Vivint maintains a safety culture in which employees share responsibility for developing and maintaining a safe working environment. Employees are responsible for completing required training, following written and verbal safety instructions, promptly reporting hazards or unsafe conditions, questioning non-standard operations or unmitigated hazards, and providing feedback on safety matters.

jobs.title: Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.

Job Overview

This position is responsible for providing supervision, direction and leadership to the operations staff including Operations Shift Leads and OMTs. Oversee daily operations activities, maintain environmental compliance and ensure that the facility is operated in a safe, reliable, and economic manner consistent with site O&M Agreement, contracts, permits, and rules and regulations written instructions from the Facility Owner. This position reports directly to the Facility Manager.

Job Responsibilities

• Direct Operations Department daily activities.

• Promote a safe working environment and ensure that all personnel and contractors follow plant and company safety procedures and policies.

• Implement programs and directives in a positive manner with a high level of confidence and commitment. Strive to address issues and/or concerns of the staff by encouraging positive thinking and a high level of productivity. Address any negative attitudes promptly and with positive reinforcement. Provide regular updates to the Facility Manager of staff morale and work ethics.

• Maintain compliance with all company policies, procedures, and contractual requirements.

• Direct plant lockout-tagout program.

• Develop and implement facility training programs for the operations personnel including cross training of facility staff to create a more flexible and productive plant environment. Provide coaching, training, and development opportunities for the team to ensure appropriate skill sets are maintained and personnel are qualified for the activities with which they are being asked to perform.

• Delegate projects and tasks to the operations personnel to maintain an acceptable backlog of work orders, work is properly distributed, and all personnel are being exposed to the various functions in the plant thus increasing the experience level of the staff.

• Support the HSE Specialist to ensure the facility environmental compliance, including the preparation of quarterly and annual reports. Interface with consultants, as needed, in the completion of environmental projects.

• Support the Facility Manager in the completion of all facility reporting requirements including environmental, safety, budgeting, and plant performance.

• Monitor and optimize plant performance. This should include periodic testing, evaluations, and recommendations to the owner for improvement projects with cost justifications. Encourage the plant staff to incorporate improvements internally to reduce contractor costs.

• Provide input and support in the development of the annual budget and annual operating plans.

• Manage the operations staff to promote efficient operations and utilization of overtime hours.

• Demonstrate effective management skills in meeting or exceeding facility goals and objectives and support the Facility Manager ensuring performance in accordance with the O&M contract.

• Maintains a productive and motivated staff through sound human resource management and the enforcement of personnel policy.

• Sets high and challenging productivity and quality standards for self and work group; encourages new ideas and work methods to lower costs and increase productivity, efficiency, quality and safety.

• Develop department training guidelines. Work with departmental personnel to ensure job/task development and knowledge base are maintained at required levels.

• Monitors inventory levels of chemicals and consumables related to operations to assure adequate supplies are available to maintain operations.

• Perform/assist in other duties as assigned by the Facility Manager.

Required Skills / Knowledge

• Demonstrates knowledge of all facets of power plant operations.

• Strong technical ability is required.

• Siemens T3000 DCS and Turbine Controls.

• Working knowledge of Zero Discharge Systems.

• Demonstrates the ability to make competent decisions in emergency situations.

• A thorough demonstrated understanding and working knowledge of operations & maintenance functions with large frame, multi-train combined cycle turbine experience is required.

• Capable of writing operating procedures, work requests, and purchase requisitions.

• Demonstrates the ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, electrical one-lines, logic drawings, technical manuals and P&ID's.

• Ion exchange de-min systems.

• Understand budgets, bid proposals, contract evaluation, basic accounting principles, plant economics and Power system operations.

• Ability to manage and motivate subordinates.

• Knowledge of Quality Programs and tools.

• Demonstrate good verbal and written communication skills.

• Will write routine reports, solve practical problems, clearly communicate tasks and needs, and train other personnel.

Experience

• A minimum of eight year's relevant experience, with a minimum of four years in a supervisory or management position or a position in which there was oversight and delegation of tasks associated with completion of projects.

• Four to six years related experience and/or training; or a combination of experience and/or education preferred.

Education Requirements

• High School diploma or equivalent required.

• Associates Degree (AA) or equivalent from a two-year college or technical school.

• A four-year degree or commensurate experience is preferred, and a demonstrated track record of successful goal achievement is required.

Physical Requirements

· Ability to do walking, reaching, climbing, and stooping and lifting (up to 50 pounds).

· From time to time the working hours will be determined on short notice based on plant requirements.

· The position requires occasional travel.

jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, LinkedIn, and follow us on Twitter @nrgenergy.

The Senior Analyst, Strategy, Performance & Transformation supports the development, execution, and performance management of Regulated customer strategy by delivering data-driven insights, financial and operational analysis, executive-ready communications, and governance support. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Customer Strategy & Transformation, with a dotted-line relationship with the Senior Manager, Strategy & Performance, this role enables both customer transformation and broader business performance priorities by translating customer, operational, financial, market, and regulatory data into actionable recommendations.

The Senior Analyst supports retention, churn reduction, customer experience improvement, strategic planning, portfolio reporting, business case development, and cross-functional initiative execution. This role helps ensure initiatives are grounded in data, aligned with regulatory and business requirements, and connected to measurable customer, operational, and financial outcomes.

Essential Duties / Responsibilities:

Support Customer Strategy Development & Insight Generation

- Analyze customer data, including retention trends, churn drivers, complaint data, and operational performance metrics to identify insights and opportunities.

- Support the development of customer segments, journeys, and experience strategies through data analysis and research.

- Translate data into clear insights and recommendations that inform strategic priorities, initiative design, and investment decisions.

- Conduct competitive, regulatory, and market analysis to support strategy development and evolution.

- Prepare analytical summaries and briefing materials to support strategic discussions and decision-making.

Enable Execution of Transformation Initiatives

- Support the translation of strategy into execution by contributing to initiative planning, including defining requirements, documenting business needs, and supporting roadmap development.

- Track initiative progress against defined milestones, identifying risks, dependencies, and delays for escalation.

- Assist in developing and maintaining project artifacts such as business requirements, process documentation, and change impact assessments.

- Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to gather inputs, validate assumptions, and ensure alignment on initiative scope and outcomes.

- Support governance processes by preparing status updates, reporting materials, and meeting documentation.

Performance Measurement & Reporting

- Monitor performance trends and identify gaps between expected and actual outcomes.

- Provide regular reporting and insights into initiative performance, highlighting key trends, risks, and opportunities.

- Support the development and refinement of KPIs to ensure alignment with business and customer experience objectives.

- Translate complex data into clear, actionable insights for both operational and leadership audiences.

Customer Retention & Experience Insights

- Analyze drivers of customer churn and retention using behavioral data, complaints, and journey analysis.

- Support the identification of root causes impacting customer experience and retention outcomes.

- Contribute to the development of retention strategies by providing data-backed insights and scenario analysis.

- Assist in evaluating the effectiveness of retention initiatives and recommending improvements.

- Support continuous improvement efforts by identifying trends and areas for optimization in customer journeys and processes.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Communication

- Partner with teams across Customer Management, Operations, Digital, Product, and Regulatory to support data collection, analysis, and initiative execution.

- Build strong working relationships with stakeholders to ensure data accuracy, alignment, and shared understanding of insights.

- Support development of executive-ready materials by synthesizing data and insights into structured narratives for senior audiences.

Support Strategic Planning & Performance Management

- Support annual and in-year strategic planning activities by consolidating inputs, preparing analysis, and developing materials that connect regional priorities to customer, operational, and financial outcomes.

- Assist with strategic reporting, including initiative status, risks, dependencies, milestones, benefits realization, and performance against defined objectives.

- Support financial and commercial analysis related to customer strategy and performance initiatives. Prepare business case inputs, financial summaries, forecasting analysis, and decision-support materials for strategic initiatives.

- Support leadership workshops and strategic discussions through preparation of analysis, materials, and meeting outputs.

Key Competencies:

- Ability to support multiple senior leaders, clarify priorities, manage ambiguity, and influence through data and structured communication

- Strong analytical, financial, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex customer, operational, and financial data and translate insights into actionable recommendations.

- Proficiency in data analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Power BI, SQL or equivalent) and presentation tools (e.g. PowerPoint)

- Strong attention to detail and data accuracy

- Comfort tracking milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions, benefits, and actions across cross-functional initiatives.

- Effective communication skills, with the ability to present insights clearly to different audiences

- Collaborative mindset with the ability to work across cross-functional teams

- Understanding of customer experience metrics (e.g., NPS, churn, retention) is an asset

- Familiarity with the Alberta natural gas or electricity industries will be considered an asset

- Experience in financial or consulting roles will be considered an asset

Minimum Requirements:

- Bachelors degree

- 3 years of industry experience or in similar roles

jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, Customer Validation
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future.

Vivint Smart Home, an NRG owned company, is a leading smart home company in the United States, dedicated to redefining the home experience with intelligent products and services. We find purpose in proactively protecting and keeping our customers connected to home, no matter where they are. Join the Smart Home team to create smarter, safer and more sustainable homes.
Position Summary

The Senior Program Manager, Customer Validation is responsible for defining and executing customer validation strategies that help ensure products are ready to deliver exceptional customer experiences before launch.

Operating as a highly autonomous individual contributor, you will serve as the customer validation subject matter expert for products moving through alpha, beta, launch readiness, and post-launch learning. You will partner closely with Product Management, Engineering, Design, Quality, Operations, and Product Research to determine what customer evidence is needed, how it should be collected, and what it means for product readiness.

This role goes beyond traditional beta program management. You will design validation strategies, define customer cohorts, develop testing methodologies, analyze customer feedback and sentiment, and provide data-driven recommendations that influence product scope, readiness, and launch decisions.

You will help transform customer validation into a scalable discipline that provides product teams with confidence they are building experiences customers will love while ensuring launch decisions are grounded in meaningful customer evidence.

Primary Responsibilities

Customer Validation Strategy & Planning

- Own customer validation strategy for products progressing through alpha, beta, launch readiness, and post-launch learning activities.

- Define validation plans, success criteria, customer cohorts, participant requirements, testing activities, and measurement approaches.

- Determine what customer evidence is required to evaluate functional readiness, customer sentiment, usability, adoption potential, and overall experience quality.

- Partner with Product Researchers to leverage research insights and translate them into later-stage validation and measurement strategies.

- Establish scalable methodologies, frameworks, and best practices for customer validation across the organization.

Alpha and Beta Program Design & Execution

- Design customer validation programs that assess both product functionality and customer experience via surveys and in lab testing.

- Develop surveys, feedback mechanisms, testing activities, and measurement plans that generate actionable customer insights.

- Partner with beta operations teams responsible for participant recruitment, fulfillment, communications, and logistics.

- Ensure validation programs accurately represent target customer populations through appropriate cohort selection and segmentation strategies.

- Identify validation risks, gaps, and dependencies while driving programs to successful completion.

Customer Insights & Readiness Recommendations

- Analyze quantitative and qualitative feedback to identify customer experience opportunities, product readiness concerns, and launch risks.

- Measure and evaluate customer sentiment, satisfaction, confidence, and perceived value in addition to product functionality.

- Synthesize customer feedback into clear recommendations for Product, Engineering, Design, and leadership teams.

- Develop executive-ready reports, readiness assessments, and customer validation summaries.

- Translate complex customer feedback into practical actions and business recommendations.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence

- Serve as the customer validation SME for assigned products and initiatives.

- Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Operations, Customer Support, and Research teams throughout the product lifecycle.

- Challenge assumptions, identify customer risks, and advocate for customer needs throughout development and launch planning.

- Escalate readiness concerns and help teams make informed decisions regarding scope, timing, and launch readiness.

- Drive alignment across stakeholders while operating with substantial autonomy and influence.

Required Skills & Functional Dimensions

- Customer Validation Expertise: Ability to translate product questions, risks, and requirements into effective customer validation strategies and programs.

- Program Leadership: Proven ability to manage complex cross-functional initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, dependencies, and timelines.

- Analytical Thinking: Strong ability to analyze customer feedback, identify meaningful patterns, and develop actionable recommendations.

- Survey & Measurement Design: Experience developing customer surveys, feedback mechanisms, and measurement frameworks that generate reliable insights.

- Technical & Product Fluency: Ability to effectively partner with Product Management and Engineering teams and translate technical requirements into customer-facing validation activities.

- Executive Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence decisions through clear, evidence-based recommendations.

- Customer Advocacy: Passion for representing the customer's perspective and ensuring customer evidence informs product decisions.

- Autonomous Execution: Ability to operate independently, define strategy, manage ambiguity, and drive outcomes with limited direction.

Required Education & Experience

- Experience: 5+ years of experience in Customer Validation, Beta Programs, Product Operations, Program Management, Product Development, Technical Program Management, or a related field.

- Cross-Functional Leadership: Demonstrated success partnering with Product, Engineering, Design, and Operations teams to deliver complex product initiatives.

- Customer Insights & Analysis: Experience analyzing customer feedback and translating data into actionable product recommendations.

- Program Development: Proven experience developing structured testing, validation, customer feedback, or product readiness programs.

- Technical Product Experience: Experience supporting the development or launch of hardware, software, platform, AI, energy, mobile, or connected product experiences.

- Education: Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, Human Factors, Psychology, Product Development, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered.

Administers plant operating budget and identifies areas of production and maintenance optimization and makes recommendations for production and maintenance improvement. Responsible for developing and tracking plant budgets using CMMS and other tools.

Job Functions:

- Leads the Operations team.

- Teams with O&M Manager-Maintenance to coordinate and execute all outages to ensure minimum down time and cost control.

- Provide leadership to all plant personnel, including regular feedback and coaching of O&M personnel as well as developing Annual Performance Reviews. Utilize the IPSC discipline procedure as appropriate in the performance of managing the O&M Personnel.

- Enhance the morale and motivation of O&M personnel. Handle employee concerns in a timely and diplomatic manner.

- Using established employee selection techniques, hires, trains and supervises all Operations O&M Technicians.

- Provides training and development opportunities for assigned personnel.

- Conduct periodic reviews of plant operations and maintenance policies and procedures to ensure they reflect current plant goals, operating requirements, and the industry's best in class

- Schedules generation, forced outages, and scheduled outages with customer.  Maintains a positive working relationship with customer.

- Develops and administers non-fuel cost of sales budget.  Provides assistance in development of capital budgets; originates authorizations for capital expenditures.

- Coordinate’s activities and interfaces with operations contractor and vendor representatives and personnel.

- Fosters an environment that encourages superior Safety awareness and Environmental Stewardship through the implementation and support of the Safety Management System and Environmental Management Systems.

- Develops, refines, and administers plant operating procedures.

- Collects, analyzes, and correlates performance data to maintain and improve plant performance.  Responsible for plant heat rate.

- Identify plant problems and improvement projects and acts as a Project Manager for the execution of approved projects.

- Manages production at facility within safe and legally permissible limits.

- Meets or exceeds daily gross margin budget.

- Establishes and maintains housekeeping standards.

- Perform economic analysis and submit budget requests as directed.

- Evaluate vendor proposals as required.

- May be assigned to Safety, Environmental or other plant committee.

- Performs several administrative tasks such as creating monthly reports, NERC compliance reporting, outage reports, etc.

- Must have hands on experience in managing contractors and plant staff during scheduled and forced outages.

- Actively promotes teamwork between the maintenance department and the operations department.

- Complete special projects as required by the Plant Manager and other leadership.

- Dependable, reliable, and predictable attendance is required for this position.

- Step up leadership as required.

Education and Experience:

- Undergraduate degree in engineering or related discipline.  Work experience may be considered in lieu of education.

- Must pass Pre-Employment drug testing and background screens.

- Minimum of five years’ supervisory experience in power generation preferred combined cycle background or similar continuous process environment.

- Experience with regulatory compliance in a continuous process environment.

- Must demonstrate proficiency in the use of computer hardware and applicable software.

- Must be able to perform physical requirements of the position including climbing ladders, stairs, and must be able to perform comprehensive site inspections.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

- Must possess basic math skills, good verbal communications skills, and be proficient with the use of power and precision tools.

- Must be cooperative with those he/she contacts in this work and have the ability to work without direct supervision.

- Must know the hazards involved and the safety precautions to be practiced in the operation and maintenance of power plant equipment and machinery.

- Work within and insure strict adherence to all safety practices and procedures.

- Must be able to respond to audio alarms and variations of sound.

- Basic data entry/computer skills

- Work as a team. Must be able to pool our knowledge and energy to work in tandem to completely understand and productively respond to all of the business challenges.

Work Environment :

- Protective equipment such as hard hats, safety glasses, air masks, ear protection and other equipment must be worn in the performance of some duties. Work with hazardous materials may be required.

- Requires working 12 hour shifts with weekend and holiday work as required by schedules, workload and plant conditions.  On call status (day and night) may be required.

- Includes working indoors and outdoors.

Physical Abilities

- Must be able to work on feet for extensive periods, requiring stair and ladder climbing, and routinely lifting 50 pounds.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Growth & Partnerships
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.

About the Role

NRG is seeking a Senior Director to join its Growth & Partnerships organization. This role is ideal for an entrepreneurial, commercially minded energy leader who enjoys building new businesses and partnerships at the intersection of customer needs, power markets, technology, capital, and enterprise strategy.

The successful candidate will combine strategic insight, commercial judgment, financial acumen, and a builder’s mindset. They will set direction for a portfolio of priority opportunities, make clear recommendations on where the organization should focus, and lead teams in testing critical assumptions. They will be accountable for advancing the most promising opportunities from growth thesis through initial market deployment and transition to scale.

This position will help shape enterprise growth opportunities across NRG’s portfolio, including data center power solutions, load management, distributed energy resources, virtual power plants, utility partnerships, generation development, edge computing, capital partnerships, and other emerging opportunities. The Senior Director will work shoulder-to-shoulder with NRG’s operating businesses and functional teams, pairing enterprise perspective with deep business-unit expertise to test, validate, and de-risk opportunities before transitioning proven models to business units for scale.

Key Responsibilities

- Lead the development of a focused pipeline of enterprise growth opportunities grounded in customer or system needs, market timing, strategic fit, partner interest, and NRG’s differentiated capabilities.

- Direct the creation and testing of growth theses by integrating customer insight, market intelligence, competitive activity, technology trends, regulatory developments, and internal expertise.

- Own the development of business cases, financial and operating models, commercialization strategies, partnership structures, and investment recommendations for priority opportunities.

- Establish the critical assumptions, value drivers, risks, dependencies, milestones, hurdle rates, and decision points required to advance opportunities with discipline.

- Lead cross-functional teams spanning commercial, finance, regulatory, legal, operations, technology, development, strategy, and business-unit organizations.

- Build trusted relationships with business-unit leaders and functional partners to identify shared priorities, mobilize expertise, and create clear pathways from enterprise incubation to scaled execution.

- Own senior external relationships with customers, utilities, technology providers, infrastructure investors, strategic capital providers, and other partners; establish the engagement strategy and guide supporting diligence, analysis, and commercial development.

- Structure initial deployments, pilots, and partnerships that test commercial models, regulatory feasibility, customer commitment, partner terms, and operating fit.

- Define measures of success and learning agendas, monitor results, and recommend whether to accelerate, reshape, partner, invest, or stop.

- Lead a small team of direct reports and mobilize cross-functional teams across the enterprise; set clear priorities and quality standards, align contributors around shared outcomes, and create an environment that rewards analytical rigor, constructive challenge, collaboration, ownership, and pace.

What We Are Looking For

- Enterprise-minded leaders who can connect capabilities across businesses and translate them into differentiated growth platforms.

- Experienced builders who can move fluidly between strategy, commercial structuring, relationship development, financial analysis, and hands-on execution.

- Deeply knowledgeable energy professionals who understand the commercial, regulatory, operational, technical, and financial forces reshaping the North American energy industry.

- Strong strategic and analytical thinkers who can develop original insights, pressure-test assumptions, and distinguish compelling ideas from scalable businesses.

- Creative problem solvers who challenge conventional thinking constructively, look around corners, and identify pragmatic paths through ambiguity.

- Commercially minded leaders who understand how customer value, competitive differentiation, execution feasibility, capital requirements, and financial returns fit together.

- Natural bridge-builders who establish trust, align diverse stakeholders, and lead effectively through influence rather than formal authority alone.

- Executive communicators who can frame decisions and present integrated recommendations to senior leadership, clearly articulating strategic fit, customer value, enterprise advantage, economics, risk, required resources, and the recommended path forward.

- People leaders who set a high bar for analytical rigor, ownership, collaboration, intellectual honesty, and pace.

Preferred Experience

- 15+ years of experience originating, structuring, and advancing new businesses, commercial models, strategic partnerships, or investment opportunities, with a demonstrated record of taking ideas from “zero to one” and playing a meaningful role in driving market or organizational change.

- Demonstrated success landing high-value partnerships, negotiating complex commercial arrangements, and advancing growth initiatives from concept through initial deployment.

- Significant leadership experience in energy, utilities, competitive power markets, customer energy solutions, distributed energy resources, energy technology, infrastructure, data centers, industrial energy management, or a closely related sector.

- Experience developing and defending complex business cases, financial models, commercial structures, and capital recommendations with senior executives and investment decision-makers.

- Track record of leading multidisciplinary teams through ambiguous, high-stakes initiatives with meaningful enterprise impact.

- Experience negotiating with customers, utilities, technology providers, strategic partners, or capital providers.

- Familiarity with several of the following areas: wholesale power and generation economics; retail energy and customer solutions; data center and hyperscaler energy needs; utility partnerships and regulation; demand response, load flexibility, DERs, and virtual power plants; corporate development; venture investing; or commercialization of new products and services.

- Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Energy Systems, Public Policy, or a related discipline.

- MBA, master’s degree, or other advanced degree preferred but not required.

Success in This Role

- Rapidly build credibility and a strong understanding of NRG’s businesses, customers, assets, capabilities, economics, and strategic priorities.

- Create a focused pipeline of differentiated growth opportunities with clear strategic relevance and enterprise advantage.

- Produce rigorous, executive-ready business cases and recommendations that enable timely capital and resource decisions.

- Build alignment across business units, functions, customers, and external partners around actionable paths forward.

- Advance priority opportunities through disciplined stage gates, initial deployment, and measurable market learning.

- Establish clear ownership and scalable transition plans for validated opportunities.

- Develop a high-performing team recognized for strategic insight, commercial judgment, analytical rigor, collaboration, and execution.

- Help NRG convert load growth, affordability needs, market evolution, and enterprise capabilities into durable sources of customer and shareholder value.

jobs.title: Director, Regulatory Compliance
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re all about propelling the next generation of leaders forward. We are driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future. We deliver innovative solutions that make our customers’ lives easier—helping them power, protect, and intelligently manage their homes and businesses. To do this, we need creative and talented people to join our company.

We offer a dynamic work environment and a unified and inclusive culture. NRG fosters a strong sense of belonging that leads to better collaboration and business performance. Our company programs are designed to help employees develop the skills they need for success now and in the future. In everything we do, we aim to champion our employees and bring value to our customers, investors and society.

More information is available at www.nrg.com. Connect with NRG on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X.

Job Summary:

The Director, Regulatory Compliance will build upon NRG’s existing trade compliance program continuing the development and implementation of a first-class program. NRG’s trading operation is regulated by a number of Federal authorities such as the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the Canada Energy Regulator (CER); and state or provincial regulators (e.g., the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCTX), Ontario Energy Board (OEB), and the Alberta Utilities Commission (AUC)). These agencies require a proactive program which, i) ensures compliance with their regulations and ii) detects and deters market manipulation. In response to these ever-evolving regulations and expansion of its trading activity from a volumetric and geographic perspective, NRG is seeking to enhance its preventative and active monitoring of trading patterns and trader behavior to minimize the potential for abusive market activity (intended or unintended).

Essential Duties/Responsibilities:

- Monitoring enforcement arms of applicable regulatory bodies, particularly FERC and CFTC to evaluate penalties assessed related to energy trading activity.

- Maintaining a comprehensive understanding of all compliance requirements relating to the Company’s energy trading activities.

- Implementing and monitoring necessary measurements to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

- Reviewing and analyzing trader transactions to identify potential areas of risk of non-compliance and proactively advise on improvements to trading behavior.

- Implement an asset bid monitoring/review program to ensure compliance with ISO/RTO market rules and market behavior rules.

- Working with support functions including Risk personnel to ensure compliance with the rules set forth by the applicable external regulatory agencies and Exchanges.

- Working with the Technical Training, Legal, and Risk teams to plan, develop, and implement training programs for personnel engaged in energy transactions to ensure compliance with rules established by the various regulatory agencies and Exchanges.

- Assisting in the development, tracking, calculating and reporting of trade compliance metrics to NRG Senior Management.

- Working with the Legal function (and others as appropriate) to conduct internal investigations, including through the review/collection/analysis of trade data, as necessary.

- Traveling periodically to participate in industry forums related to energy trading, or to collaborate with NRG personnel located outside of primary office location as necessary.

Working Conditions:

- Position location is in Houston, TX.

Minimum Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in a related field of study.

- Minimum of eight (8) years of directly related experience in energy trading, or in a compliance role at an exchange, ISO/RTO, or governmental regulatory oversight body is required.

- Knowledge of trading operations, trade practices, and/or rules and regulations related to trading on a Designated Contract Market (DCM) is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Advanced degree is a plus, but is not required.

- Understanding of swaps and derivatives as used in the energy industry and how such trading activities may interact to create the appearance of market manipulation.

- Knowledge of ISO/RTO power products (including FTRs and virtual transactions), trading strategies and protocols.

- Knowledge of power and natural gas trading strategies and protocols, and regulations.

- Detailed knowledge of major external regulations applicable to energy trading, including the Commodity Exchange Act, FERC Order 670, Prohibition of Energy Market Manipulation, and FERC’s gas pipeline capacity release rules.

- Demonstrated experience with FERC’s Office of Enforcement and its views on market manipulation.

- Experience with Nasdaq’s SMARTS, Aligne, or trade capture systems in general is a plus.

- Additional Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

- Aggressive, analytical self-manager with critical thinking skills and keen judgment.

- Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate (verbal and written) with all levels of internal or external groups.

- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work in both team environments and independently.

- Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Microsoft Teams.

jobs.title: Hardware Strategic Sourcing Manager
jobs.description:
Welcome to the intersection of energy and home services. At NRG, we’re driven by our passion to create a smarter, cleaner and more connected future.

Vivint Smart Home, an NRG owned company, is a leading smart home company in the United States, dedicated to redefining the home experience with intelligent products and services. We find purpose in proactively protecting and keeping our customers connected to home, no matter where they are. Join the Smart Home team to create smarter, safer and more sustainable homes.
Who Are We:

Vivint LLC is a leading smart home company in North America. Vivint delivers an integrated smart home system with in-home consultation, professional installation and support delivered by its Smart Home Pros, as well as 24-7 customer care and monitoring. Dedicated to redefining the home experience with intelligent products and services, Vivint serves more than 1.4 million customers throughout the U.S. and Canada. Vivint is on the Forbes 2018 list of “America’s Best Employers, as well as the Forbes 2019 list of “America’s Best Employers for Diversity.” The company is the largest tech employer in Utah, a certified Great Place to Work, and one of Fast Company’s World’s 50 Most Innovative Companies for 2017. For more information, visit  www.vivint.com .

Vivint is looking for a Hardware Strategic Sourcing Manager to be responsible for managing supplier costs, contracts, relationships, and roadmaps. The position will also play a lead role in representing the Supply Chain Organization in the new product introduction (NPI) process. In this role, the individual will lead supplier sourcing and selection activities and be responsible for managing the supplier relationship. It will be critical for the individual to develop close collaboration with Hardware Engineering, Program Management, Technical Operations, and other cross- functional teams. During the product development process, you are responsible for ensuring the suppliers are prepared to support the delivery of key parts on-time at specified quality, and yield parameters and are prepared to meet the ramp quantities. It is the Sourcing Manager’s primary objective to ensure suppliers meet or exceed commercial and technical requirements throughout the life cycle of the product(s).

For assigned suppliers and programs this role is expected to:

- Have strong organization and communication skills

- Standardize effective/efficient/repeatable supply chain processes

- Develop and own supplier/commodity/category sourcing strategies, ensuring that suppliers are capable of meeting Vivint’s current and future technical and business requirements

- Establish supplier selection criteria, evaluate alternative suppliers, manage the RFQ process, and drive final supplier selection in partnership with Product Management, Engineering, Quality, and other cross-functional partners

- Properly prepare for and negotiate various agreements as needed with suppliers to establish best-in-class pricing, flexibility, quality, delivery, payment, warranty, and service terms

- Formulate contingency plans to de-risk technical challenges, long lead time, single source, and any supply issue

- Institute programs to optimize schedule flexibility while minimizing excess inventory exposure · Work with CM partners to resolve any part shortages or quality problems which affects production schedules

- Own, manage, and approve the ramp plan, ongoing production plan and forecast, tooling qualification schedule and tooling life for all designated suppliers

- Influence supplier technology roadmaps and create internal disruptive value-add to ensure Vivint’s system architecture and commercial requirements are met

- Establish and manage strategic supplier relationships at the executive level

- Provide interdepartmental program updates on cost, schedule, design, supplier issues, quality, risk, etc.

- Manage regular business reviews of strategic sourcing plan that define product roadmaps, supplier capabilities and annual / quarterly strategic business objectives

- Maintain personal knowledge of market trends including rigorous analysis of market drivers, cost structures and technical improvements

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain Management or Engineering or equivalent work experience.

- 5-7 years' experience in high volume manufacturing operations or sourcing environment.

- 5-7 years direct experience in supplier / supply chain management

- Supply chain experience managing cross functional teams in a consumer electronics product company.

- Familiarity with world-class sourcing methods and tools.

- Ability to solve problems and coordinate with cross-functional teams.

- Ability to be innovative in issues related to strategic sourcing, vendor relations, quality assurance and the associated measurement systems.

- Strong analytical skills (i.e. cost modeling, quotation analysis, supplier selection).

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- Master's degree.

- Excellent written and verbal communications skills.

- Fluent in English; Mandarin, Vietnamese, or Thai are a plus.

Job Functions:

Position requires in-office presence in Seattle, WA on a hybrid schedule for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday with a work from home day on Friday. The position will start remote and then will move into the hybrid schedule.

What We Stand For:

Honesty and Integrity Come First - Do the right thing

Customer Obsession is Our Advantage - A relentless passion to serve the customer Innovation is Essential - Today’s innovation is tomorrow’s lifeblood

We Win Together - Individuals win games: teams win championships

Exceptional is Expected - Talk is cheap: create value, not just motion

We Give Back - Helping people is core to our DNA
